Messages.Author: Peter Mazarakos
Messages.Body:
Paul Jensen (pjensen@orion.it.luc.edu) wrote:
: LANspeed (lanspeed@coyote.rain.org) wrote:
: :         In a recent game I bum rushed one of my prey's minions with a
: : brujah that had superior celerity and potence. During the strike phase I
: : played Fists of Death which gave me +2 damage but cost 1 blood from my
: : vampire and Blur which game me 2 addtitional strikes but cost 1. (I
: : thought it was pretty cool, until) I payed the blood and had put the cards
: : in my ash pile, when my opponet played Majesty or some combat ends stike.
: :         Now my question is do I get either cards back or either of the
: : blood? It seems that I wouldn't have exerted myself to the point where I
: : would have to pay any blood for either of those skills if I nveer used
: : them. Maybe turning my fists into fists of death would cost me one, but
: : wouldn't that happen during combat...not as I chose my strikes. Well
: : anyway...any feedback is welcome

: Well it seems to me that you did everything right except one, which ended up
: costing you some blood.  For combat cards, I've always understood the rules to
: be that you pay the blood, when they are played--immediately.  I think this
: is the bonus of having combat ends, cards--your opponent pays for a combat card
: and gets nothing out of it.  However,  Blur is *not* a strike cards, or you
: would not have been able to play it as you can only play *one* strike card
: a strike phase.  Blur is an additional strike card and is played on the combat
: phase after damage resolution.  In the situtation stated above, I think you
: used Blur a little to early.  It should have gone like this:

: 1. Manuver (no manuvers)
: 2. Strike (Fists of Death , Majesty)
: if no Majesty had been played
: 3. Resolve Damage
: 4. Additional Strikes (Blur)
: 5. Press

: By playing the Blur out of turn you lost the extra blood for the Blur.
: I hope this makes sense.
: --

: |      Chicago, IL                                  |
: +---------------------------------------------------+
: |      Good advertising space for rent              |
: |      (It must be pretty good YOU just read it)    |

I was under the impression that strike resolution came after ALL strikes.
If you played blur, your additional strikes would all be resolved at the
same time as the first one.

1. Manuver
2. Strike
3. Additional strikes
4. Strike resolution
5. Press

This way, you can blur your flamethower and get in extra strikes.  Makes
sense, no?

Messages.Author: Eric Amick
Messages.Body:
Peter Mazarakos (pmazarak@snoqualmie.eecs.uic.edu) wrote:

>I was under the impression that strike resolution came after ALL strikes.
>If you played blur, your additional strikes would all be resolved at the
>same time as the first one.

>1. Manuver
>2. Strike
>3. Additional strikes
>4. Strike resolution
>5. Press

>This way, you can blur your flamethower and get in extra strikes.  Makes
>sense, no?

Um, no.  The original and corrected rules both list additional strikes as
happening after the resolution of the initial strike, and each additional
strike also has its own distinct choose strike and resolve strike phases.

the first strike.  Are you telling me that the first time they get nicked by

supposed to burn people in combat? :-(  (My favourite!)

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Craig Thomas Judd <cjudd@lawson.its.utas.edu.au> wrote:
>So what's the point of having an aggravated-damage weapon that hits each
>strike?...

The usefulness is that you don't have to keep playing aggravation cards
like Wolf Claws over and over again.  The other players know that if they
get into combat with that minion and can't avoid or prevent the damage,
their minion *will* be going to torpor.

>Are you telling me that the first time they get nicked by
>an aggravated strike, they fall over so you can't do it to them again?! >:-D

Not until they get back out of torpor again, no.

>Granted, that IS the way it states in the rules, I guess - but how are you
>supposed to burn people in combat? :-(  (My favourite!)

Doing lots and lots of aggravated damage all at once.
Torn Signpost/Growing Fury/Wolf Claws, for example  :)

Messages.Author: Jeff Siegal
Messages.Body:
I thought the rules state:
(Summarized) The first point of aggravated damage shocks the vampires system and sends him to torpor.  This is not healed by spending the vampires blood.  Each additional point of aggravated damage is then healed within torpor so the vampire spends blood to heal that. if the vampire has no blood to heal the excess aggravated damage it is burned and placed in the ash heap.
That's what it says, and seems reasonable to play that way.

Messages.Author: David Q. Spitzley
Messages.Body:
Well, if you notice, damage from one strike is applied before either
additional strikes or presses.  As a result, a single hit doing
aggravated damage ends the entire combat.  So, go up against a vampire
with a flamethrower, go to torpor before he can finish you off.
Again, run the combat round sequence rules past the other players.  It's
in there.  If they whine about it being to hard to kill vampires then,
